items.title: [model] fix: Ulysses SP support for Qwen3.5/Qwen3.5-MoE
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Fix

Two bugs prevent Ulysses Sequence Parallelism (SP > 1) from working
with Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.5-MoE models:

1. `_ulysses_flash_attention_forward` passes sliced `position_ids`
   (a non-contiguous view) directly to `all_gather`, which requires
   contiguous tensors. Crashes with
   `RuntimeError: Tensors must be contiguous` at step 0.

2. `patch_vlm_for_ulysses_input_slicing` was never registered for
   `Qwen3_5TextModel` / `Qwen3_5MoeTextModel`. Other VLMs (Qwen2.5VL,
   Qwen3VL, GLM4V) all have this Step 3 registration; Qwen3.5 was
   the only one missing it. Without it, `inputs_embeds` and
   `position_ids` are not sliced per SP rank, causing shape mismatch
   in the forward pass.

## Relation to #5957 and #6094

#5957 reports shape mismatch (`logits_rmpad` vs `temperature_rmpad`)
on NPU with Qwen3.5 + SP > 1. #6094 reports SP works for Qwen-3 but
fails for Qwen-3.5 with tensor shape mismatch. Both share the same
root cause: missing `patch_vlm_for_ulysses_input_slicing` for Qwen3.5.

## Duplicate-work check

```
gh pr list --repo verl-project/verl --state open --search "patch_vlm_for_ulysses"
gh pr list --repo verl-project/verl --state open --search "position_ids contiguous"
```

First query returns no results. Second returns #5886 and #5829 which
address different issues (nested tensor / mrope), not the Ulysses SP
`all_gather` path.

## Test plan

- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B GRPO + Ulysses SP=2 + FSDP2 param_offload,
  10x Ascend 910B.
- Without fix 1: `RuntimeError: Tensors must be contiguous` at step 0
  `compute_log_prob`.
- Without fix 2: shape mismatch -- `inputs_embeds` not sliced per rank.
- With both fixes: training completes step 1 with correct metrics.
- `pre-commit run --files verl/models/transformers/monkey_patch.py`:
  all hooks pass.

## AI-assisted disclosure

AI assistance (Claude) used. Submitter reviewed every changed line.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

Closes #6424 (and the three sibling issues #4757 / #6223 / #6252 that share the same root cause).

The agent loop's token-in-token-out pipeline has been `apply chat template → generate() → decode → tool parser` with no reasoning-parser step in between. Reasoning models (Qwen3 thinking, DeepSeek-R1, GLM-4 thinking) often emit `<tool_call>` patterns *inside* `<think>...</think>` blocks as part of their chain of thought. The regex-based `ToolParser` then treats those think-block tool calls as real invocations and executes them during training — polluting the conversation history (#4757), teaching the model that loose tool-call placement is acceptable, and triggering benchmark regression once eval harnesses use stricter parsing (#6223 / #6252).

This PR adds an **opt-in** reasoning-parser step that mirrors what vLLM and SGLang already apply on the chat-completion serving path:

```
generate() → decode → reasoning_parser → tool_parser → execute
```

`reasoning_parser=None` (the default) keeps the legacy behavior, so existing pipelines are unchanged.

items.title: [model] fix: DSA for mcore >= 0.16.2: route x/qr kwargs and add PyTorch WHT fa…
items.bodyExcerpt:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes MultiLatentAttention (DSA variant) compatibility with mcore ≥ 0.16.2 and adds a pure-PyTorch Walsh-Hadamard fallback for environments that don't have the fast_hadamard_transform CUDA extension.

**Background**. verl patches MultiLatentAttention.forward to forward extra kwargs (x, qr) that DSA's core_attention requires. In mcore ≤ 0.16.1 this patch replaced the upstream forward unconditionally. Starting from mcore 0.16.2, the upstream MultiLatentAttention.forward was restructured (packed-seq + CP support), so applying the verl patch wholesale breaks standard MLA. Additionally, mcore's DSA module imports fast_hadamard_transform at module load time and silently sets hadamard_transform = None when the C extension is absent — causing a crash at the first DSA forward pass.

Changes:
1. For mcore ≥ 0.16.2, route only DSA instances (experimental_attention_variant == "dsa") through patch_forward; leave standard MLA on the upstream forward.
2. Inject a pure-PyTorch Walsh-Hadamard transform into the DSA module namespace when hadamard_transform is None, so DSA runs without the fast_hadamard_transform package.
3. Move private megatron/torch imports in apply_patch_megatron_v012_with_torch_v28_v29 behind the version guard to prevent ImportError on installations that don't have those internal APIs.

### Test

Validated by running GLM-5.1 (744B MoE, glm_moe_dsa model type, DSA attention) end-to-end training with Megatron backend on mcore 0.16.2. Without the patch, the forward pass crashes immediately; with the patch, training proceeds normally.

Standard MLA models are unaffected: the _forward_dsa_compat wrapper checks experimental_attention_variant and falls through to the upstream forward for all non-DSA instances.

items.title: [model] fix: treat position_ids as optional in Ulysses input slicing
items.bodyExcerpt:
### What does this PR do?

Ulysses sequence parallelism crashes instead of running when the caller does not pass
`position_ids`.

`patch_vlm_for_ulysses_input_slicing` decides whether to slice based on `inputs_embeds` alone,
then slices `position_ids` unconditionally:

```python
slice_now = (
    inputs_embeds is not None
    and current_ulysses_sp_size > 1
    and getattr(self, "_needs_initial_slice", True)
)
if slice_now:
    call_kwargs["inputs_embeds"] = slice_input_tensor(inputs_embeds, dim=1, padding=False)
    call_kwargs["position_ids"] = slice_input_tensor(position_ids, dim=-1, padding=False)
```

`position_ids` is optional in transformers — omit it and the model derives positions from the
sequence length it is handed. `slice_input_tensor` reads `x.size(dim)` on its first line, so
omitting it gives:

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size'
```

Minimal reproduction, with the wrapper installed on a stand-in module and slicing done without a
process group:

```
inputs_embeds + position_ids   ->  (1, 64, 8) -> (1, 32, 8),  (1, 64) -> (1, 32)     ok
inputs_embeds only             ->  AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size'
```

`patch_vlm_for_ulysses_input_slicing` is installed for `qwen2_vl`, `qwen3_vl`, `qwen3_vl_moe`,
`glm4v`, `kimi_vl`, `qwen3_5` and `qwen3_5_moe`, so this is on the shared sequence-parallel path
rather than one model's.

### The change

Slice `position_ids` only when there is one. Nothing else moves.

Leaving it unsliced is also the correct value rather than a workaround: the embeddings passed
down are already this rank's shard, so positions the model derives from their length are exactly
the ones this rank should see. Slicing a full-length `position_ids` and slicing nothing both end
at the same per-rank positions; the difference is only whether the caller supplied them.

items.title: [Bug]: b12x NSA+MTP speculative decoding hangs on PCIe TP=8 — NCCL topology-aware scheduling fix
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, PCIe-only TP=8, Ubuntu 24.04, vLLM main + b12x

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Bug: b12x NSA + MTP speculative decoding hangs on PCIe TP=8

When running GLM-5.1 or Kimi-K2.6 with b12x `B12X_MLA_SPARSE` backend + MTP speculative decoding on PCIe-only 8-GPU setup (TP=8, no NVLink), vLLM **always hangs** during decode. This is not intermittent — it is deterministic.

### Root Cause

Three layers of conflict:

1. **NCCL on PCIe topology**: NCCL's default ring/tree communication pattern conflicts with b12x's barrier sync. During MTP verify, the all-reduce for draft token scoring and b12x's cross-GPU KV sync compete for the same PCIe bandwidth. Timing skew → deadlock.

2. **b12x scheduling vs MTP dynamic batch**: b12x's CUDA Graph requires fixed input shapes and static `page_table_1` layout. MTP verify produces variable-length accepted tokens, causing `nsa_cache_seqlens` to diverge from graph-captured state at replay time.

3. **NSA indexer dangling indices**: Draft tokens write temporary KV entries. If verify rejects them, KV cache rolls back but `topk_indices` from the indexer still reference the now-invalid entries → garbage attention output (e.g. XML tag leakage in tool calls).

### Fix

1. **NCCL patch**: Force NCCL to respect PCIe topology — route collective operations along the actual PCIe switch hierarchy instead of assuming uniform interconnect. This prevents barrier misalignment between MTP verify all-reduce and b12x KV sync.

2. **Rewrite b12x scheduling logic**: Replace the static CUDA-Graph-only decode path with a topology-aware scheduler that dynamically selects execution path based on current phase (draft / verify / committed). With HiSparse mixed DRAM/VRAM NIXL reads, this also prevents the decode worker from sending completion notifications to prefill, leaving prefill waiting for remote cleanup during its own pause.

The deployment that exposed this uses GLM-5.3, B300, DP/EP=8 per replica, NIXL P/D, HiSparse on decode, and MooncakeStore through MultiConnector. 1. D has a request in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`, in `waiting` or `skipped_waiting`.

Mixed-memory software notification bookkeeping was introduced by #53780 and is exercised by the HiSparse path. Port [ROCm/ATOM#788](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/pull/788)'s indexer fused-kernel shape into vLLM. Replaces the `k_norm → rotary_emb → per_token_group_quant_fp8 → cache` chain (and the Q-side `per_token_group_quant_fp8`) inside `Indexer.forward` with a single AITER kernel `aiter.indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` (ROCm/aiter#3185, correctness fixes in ROCm/aiter#3451).

> **Companion:** ROCm/aiter#3451 — required. Without it GSM8K strict-match drops 0.95 → 0.49.

## Gating

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_DSV32_INDEXER_FUSION` (default off) + main AITER toggle; auto-disabled when the running AITER build does not expose `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache`. The kernel hard-asserts `index_head_dim == 128`, `qk_rope_head_dim == 64`, `head_dim == quant_block_size`; `Indexer.__init__` only enables the path if all three hold and `model_type != "glm_moe_dsa"`.

## Design notes

- **Stays inside the existing custom op.** Calling the fused kernel from inside `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer` keeps `q_fp8` and `weights_out` from escaping — an earlier version that registered them as a separate op leaked pointers across piecewise-cudagraph segments and tanked GSM8K to ~1%.
- **Persistent workspace** for `q_fp8` / `weights_out`, grown monotonically. Otherwise 61 indexer layers × 2 allocations per decode step churn the eager allocator.
- **K stride fixup.** The kernel asserts `k.stride(0) == head_dim`, but the upstream `.contiguous()` is a no-op on `size(0) == 1` views. We rewrite the metadata via `as_strided` when it's safe, else `empty + copy_`.
- **`preshuffle=True`.** Downstream consumers read MFMA 16×16 SHUFFLE; the original call site passed `False` and silently produced garbage. Bytewise-equal to the unfused triton write after the fix.
- **fp32 LN params** passed through as-is (required by ROCm/aiter#3451).

## Purpose

Fuse the clamped MoE activation path into FP8 block-128 activation quantization:

1. finite SwiGLU clamping;
2. BF16 SiLU and gated multiplication;
3. dynamic E4M3 block quantization, including Hopper DeepGEMM UE8M0 scales; and
4. optional filtering of invalid or non-local expert rows.

The CUDA implementation extends the existing stable-ABI `silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` op and has two execution strategies:

- a lightweight one-block-per-quant-group kernel for launch-bound TP decode shapes without an `expert_map`;
- an occupancy-driven persistent kernel when EP filtering is present or the output has at least 1M elements.

The persistent variant uses vectorized BF16 loads/FP8 stores and half-warp reductions. Both clamped variants preserve the BF16 activation materialization point and are bit-exact with the original two-kernel UE8M0 path.

The Triton experts dispatch remains narrow: CUDA, gated SiLU with a finite clamp, int32 routing IDs, FP8 W8A8 block shape `[128, 128]`, and no LoRA activation consumer. Large unfiltered prefills fall back to the existing kernels at the measured crossover. ## Purpose

Adds an AITER-backed fusion path for the ROCm `deepseek_v32` (DeepSeek Sparse
Attention) forward, used by both DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.2. The existing
shared-Triton fusion path is untouched and remains the default; the AITER path
is selected at runtime per fusion via opt-in env flags, so behaviour on ROCm is
unchanged unless a flag is set.

This PR is stacked on top of: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51915, so needs enablement to land first before this fusion add-on.

### Fusions added

**1. MLA dual RMSNorm** 
Fuses the q and kv-a RMSNorms into one AITER call
(`fused_mla_dual_rms_norm_out`). An out-variant was added so the norms write
model-owned buffers rather than allocating per layer, which lets the call be
hoisted out of the eager region and captured by cudagraph. Also wires the
per-token-quant variant for the quantized case.

**2. Fused QK RoPE + concat + MLA cache write** 
`rocm_aiter_fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` replaces the separate RoPE,
concat and KV-cache-write steps on the MLA path. The uint8 KV cache allocated by
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` is viewed as `float8_e4m3fn` before the call, since the
AITER op rejects the raw uint8 buffer.

**3. Fused indexer QK RoPE + fp8 quant + cache write**
`rocm_aiter_indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` fuses the lightning-indexer key
LayerNorm, RoPE, fp8 quantization, and cache write into one call for the 21
indexer layers.

**4. Fused all-reduce + RMSNorm**
Uses AITER's custom all-reduce with an in-kernel RMSNorm. Gated on custom-AR
eligibility (`should_custom_ar`) because the op asserts the kernel ran, and
oversized batches must fall back to the standard path — this is the check the
torch.compile pass performs at compile time and which an inline call has to do
itself.

This change adds an exact target-token path for V2/MRV2 GLM

## Purpose

A deterministic `persistent_topk` (the QSA / sparse-indexer block selection,
`csrc/libtorch_stable/persistent_topk.cuh`) that is **also faster than the exact-topk workaround**
people currently reach for. The kernel returns a different result for identical inputs from call to
call: the **order** always varies, and when more keys share the threshold value than the candidate
buffers hold, the selected **set** varies too. Cause: output slots are handed out by `atomicAdd` in
thread-arrival order, and exact-key ties at the last radix round are taken first-come.

cache is allocated as `uint8` storage and `run()` views it as `float8_e4m3fn`, but
`plan()` was handed the storage dtype, which the FlashInfer wrapper rejects:
`ValueError: MLA kv_data_type torch.uint8 is not supported`. One-line dtype fix in
`FlashInferMLASparseSM90Builder`.

**2. The indexer prefill workspace is sized in the wrong unit.**
`get_max_prefill_buffer_size()` returns a token count (`max_model_len * 40` entries of
132 bytes), but this indexer's KV is pool-granular: the spec carries
`compress_ratio == index_kpool`, and `split_indexer_prefill_chunks()` is fed compressed
sequence lengths. `deepseek_v4/attention.py` already divides at the same call site.
At `--max-model-len 1048576` with `index_kpool = 4` this locks ~5.16 GiB per GPU during
the memory profile, straight out of the KV budget. Reported by @nood-co1 in #53906.

- #54743 scopes offload group configs to prefix-cacheable groups; different file,
  different failure.
- Searched open PRs for `get_max_prefill_buffer_size`, `max_total_seq_len` and the SM90

No unit test covers either path (both need a GLM-5.3 checkpoint and FlashInfer on
Hopper), so this was validated by serving. 2x H200 NVL, TP2, LibertAI NVFP4 weights,

## 🚀 Description

Enables `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache for rope-free NoPE sparse-MLA models (`qk_rope_head_dim=0`, head_dim 512, e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash) on **SM90/Hopper** via the FlashMLA sparse backend, served through a zero-padded 576/656B envelope.

Today on H200, GLM-5.3-Flash must either use bf16 KV (~2x memory) or the plain per-tensor-fp8 `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` backend, which returns no LSE and therefore cannot run DCP (decode context parallel) or compose with the MTP fused-draft path. items.title: [Spec Decode] GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash2 aux hidden-state capture
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Enable DFlash2 speculative decoding for GLM-5.3-Flash by implementing aux hidden-state capture on the target model. Related: #55423 (same goal, different aux-materialization path — see below; comment posted there with the structural analysis).

## Problem

#55423 materializes aux states as `hidden + residual`. GLM's mHC residual is a deferred-fusion structure: at each layer boundary the decoder holds a 4-tuple `(x, residual, post, comb)`, and the layer-k output is only completed by `MHCPostOp` (`mhc.py`), whose mixing weights live inside the `post/comb` tensors. A plain `hidden + residual` therefore captures an intermediate state, not the completed output of layer k that the draft was trained against. We believe this may explain the unisolated output divergence reported in #55423.

## Solution

Capture before layer k+1, materializing aux via `hc_post(x, residual, post, comb)` followed by `hc_contract` — structurally identical to the last-layer epilogue. KDA/non-mHC boundaries fall back to `hidden + residual`. Sequence-parallel gather skips the dense stages. The multimodal wrapper (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, the architecture of the official `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` checkpoint) declares `SupportsEagle3` and delegates to the inner text model, so the protocol unpack through `language_model.model` works natively.

Semantics adapted from SGLang `xinyuan/glm-5.3-flash-support` (#36507/#36708), Apache-2.0.

## Summary

- route rope-free sparse MLA to the ROCm Triton implementation for every KV-cache dtype
- dequantize FP8 KV rows in the Triton ragged-prefill kernel using the layer KV scale while keeping Q in model dtype

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

For a hybrid (Mamba / linear-attention) model with speculative decoding, `MambaSpec.max_memory_usage_bytes` charges each request `num_speculative_blocks` extra state pages per Mamba group. In `align` mode:

```python
return self.page_size_bytes * (
    2 + self.num_speculative_blocks + self.num_prefill_checkpoint_blocks
)
```

`get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config` then divides the whole block pool by that per-request footprint — so the drafting scratch is reserved **once per KV-concurrency slot**.

items.title: [Feature] Restore concurrent partial prefill limit (max_concurrent_prefills) in V1 scheduler
items.bodyExcerpt:
Reviving #55256's clean threshold-independent `max_concurrent_prefills` limit for the V1 scheduler to fix the exact head-of-line blocking issue reported in #57413.

As detailed in #57413, without a cap on concurrent partial prefills, long-context RAG workloads (e.g. 100k+ tokens) completely stall V1's scheduling queue. Short requests are forced to wait for many iterations until massive partial prefills finish.

This reintroduces `max_concurrent_prefills` directly into the V1 scheduler's `WAITING` loop. By bounding how many requests can simultaneously hold partial prefill state, we allow interleaving and dramatically reduce tail TTFT (as validated by the community on 4x B200 / GLM-5.3-Flash).

## Summary

This PR adds a correctness-first CPU execution path for GLM-5.3-Flash / GLM5Next KDA for #57346.

The path is deliberately feature-local:

```text
GLM5Next common KDA layer
  -> CPU platform dispatch
  -> CPU state helpers and causal convolution
  -> CPU KDA recurrence/chunk contract
  -> optional _C_AVX512 recurrent operator
```

### Scope and design

The initial source audit showed that CPU support required more than changing the two KDA imports. The common layer also reaches causal-convolution and state gather/scatter boundaries that have GPU-oriented implementations. The related CPU GDN implementation was used as a reference for stateful CPU integration, but it was not treated as a drop-in KDA implementation. KDA differs in safe-gate semantics, beta handling, V-major state layout, and speculative state routing.

items.title: [Bugfix] Invalidate KDA merged conv-weight cache on weight reload
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087. GLM-5.3 KDA merges the q/k/v short-conv weights into one cached tensor (`_merged_conv_weight`), built lazily on first forward. Online-RL workflows warm up with dummy weights (cache built), then refit `q_conv1d`/`k_conv1d`/`v_conv1d` — but the cached merge is never invalidated, so inference silently keeps using the pre-refit convolution weights.

## Approach

Weight loading dispatches on the param's stamped `weight_loader` (`getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)` in `AutoWeightsLoader`). So the cache can be invalidated at exactly the point the weights change: in `Glm5NextLinearAttention.__init__`, wrap each conv weight's stamped loader so any write clears `_merged_conv_weight`. The next forward rebuilds it from the current params. No new hooks, no changes to the reload machinery.

## Coverage / limitations

- ✅ Initial load (loaders run before first forward; cache built after anyway)
- ✅ Checkpoint-format refit: `reload_weights` → `model.load_weights` → stamped loaders → cache cleared
- ✅ Layerwise reload: re-dispatches through the same stamped loaders
- ❌ Kernel-format refit (`param.copy_` bypass) writes params without loaders — the cache is NOT invalidated there. That path also skips every other derived-weight rebuild in the tree (same class of limitation); noted for follow-up if it matters in practice.

items.title: [Bugfix] Skip FP8-dequant fast paths for PP-missing layers in GLM-5.3-Flash load
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55725. GLM-5.3-Flash crashes at weight load on multi-node (2×8 H100) with `KeyError: 'layers.11.self_attn.fused_qkv_a_proj.weight'` on every second-node worker, while single-node runs fine.

## Root cause

With 2 nodes the run is pipeline-parallel (PP=2), so layer 11's params exist only on stage-0 ranks. The attached log (`layer11.log`) shows all `Worker_PP1_TP0..7` crashing; PP0 is clean. The normal load path guards every weight with `is_pp_missing_parameter` (glm5next/common/model.py), but the two FP8-dequant fast paths bypass it and index `params_dict` directly:

- `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj` → `params_dict[target_w]` (the traceback in the issue)
- `_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk` → `params_dict[fused_name]` (same class of hole)

On a PP rank that doesn't hold the layer, `params_dict` has no such key → KeyError before the normal path ever gets a chance to skip the weight.

## Fix

In both fast paths, return `False` when the target param is absent from `params_dict`, so the weight falls through to the normal path, which skips it via `is_pp_missing_parameter`. The indexer-wk guard is placed *before* buffering, so PP ranks also don't accumulate fp8 tensors that nobody loads. Behavior on ranks that hold the layer is byte-identical.

## Verification

No multi-node GPU here, so verified by driving both functions directly with the exact crashing weight names, on the MI350X pod against the patched module:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| PP1-style params_dict (layer 11 absent), fp8 `q_a_proj` weight + scale | not consumed, nothing loaded → falls to normal skip path (was: KeyError) |
| PP0-style control (BF16 `fused_qkv_a_proj` present) | consumed + loaded, unchanged |
| PP1, indexer `wk` weight + scale | not consumed → normal skip |
| PP0 control, indexer `wk` | consumed + loaded, unchanged |

Pre-commit: all hooks pass. Single-node (TP-only) behavior is untouched — the guards only trigger when the target param is missing.

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix Whisper engine crash on audio clips longer than 30s
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Offline `LLM.generate` with Whisper and an audio clip longer than 30 s kills the engine on main and on v0.29.0:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1750) must match the size of tensor b (1500) at non-singleton dimension 0
```

Every later request then fails with `EngineDeadError`. v0.26.0 accepts the same input and truncates the clip to 30 s, which is what the HF feature extractor does by default.

The cause is the same as in #56912 (Qwen2-Audio). Since #53275 the multimodal processor passes `truncation=False` to the HF processor so that the placeholder text is not cut. `WhisperProcessor` forwards the same kwarg to `WhisperFeatureExtractor`, which then stops truncating audio to its 30 s window. A 35 s clip becomes 3500 frames, which is 1750 positions after the conv, and the encoder has 1500.

The fix is the same line as in #56912: `WhisperMultiModalProcessor._get_hf_mm_inputs` passes `truncation=True`. Clips of up to 30 s are processed exactly as before.

`/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/v1/audio/translations` are not affected, because the server splits audio into chunks of at most 30 s before it reaches the processor, and Whisper does not serve the other endpoints. Only offline use with a longer clip hits this.

I did not find an existing issue or PR for this (searched for whisper truncation, whisper 30s, and the error message). Of the other audio models I could load, GLM-ASR and Qwen3-ASR handle long clips correctly and Qwen2-Audio is already fixed. I have not checked the rest.

items.title: [Perf][HiSparse] Avoid repeated prefix scans and residency updates
items.bodyExcerpt:
HiSparse's scheduler rescans the entire computed prefix on every materialization call, including pages already known to be durable. Each resident cache group also invokes the same shared materialization and residency operations. With 20 resident groups and hundreds of requests per rank, this consumed most of a scheduler CPU core and delayed workers before their DP collective.

This patch starts scanning at `max(ready_prefix_pages, importing_pages)` and invokes the shared operations only from the first resident manager. It preserves pending-write checks, holes beyond the durable prefix, spill budgets, import completion, and publication ordering. No serving configuration, routing, graph policy, or model math changes are included.

Two existing materialization tests now exercise both one and three resident groups, covering incomplete/out-of-order writes and per-step spill budgets.

### Performance evidence

B300, one EP8 prefill node and one EP8 decode node, 2,048-concurrent Scale-SWE agentic rollouts. GLM-5.3 NVFP4 (`RadixArk/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`, revision `11af4cba759e6559eda70358a5778bd1bddddd78`), FP8 KV, HiSparse 300 GiB/decode GPU, index cache, NIXL and Mooncake, Rust frontend, natural routing. Decode used DeepEP LL and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE breakable graphs; EPLB, DBO and speculative decoding were disabled.

items.title: [Bugfix] Make disable_any_whitespace actually disable whitespace on xgrammar
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`disable_any_whitespace` does not disable whitespace on the xgrammar backend — it **makes whitespace mandatory**, and as a side effect masks out the token the model wants at every JSON value position.

xgrammar's `any_whitespace=False` selects a *fixed* JSON format rather than a whitespace-free one. Its docstring is explicit that the format follows `json.dumps()` conventions, and with `separators` left unset the default is `(", ", ": ")` — *with* spaces. `backend_xgrammar.py` never passes `separators`, so today the flag requires a space after every comma and colon.

The second-order effect is the damaging one. Because the space is mandatory, the bare `"` that opens a string value becomes illegal at the value position. Measured on the mask with a real GLM-5.3 tokenizer, immediately after `{"location":`:

| grammar config | allowed tokens | whitespace-leading | bare `"` | digit-leading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `any_whitespace=True` | 1450 | 719 | yes | 395 |
| `any_whitespace=False`, default separators — **today** | 268 | **268, all of them** | **banned** | 0 |
| `any_whitespace=False`, `separators=(",", ":")` — **this PR** | 703 | **0** | yes | 395 |

The middle row is what vLLM produces now: every legal continuation begins with a space. A model prompted for minified JSON wants the bare `"`; with it masked out, probability mass shifts to the whitespace-prefixed set, where `␣0`, `␣1`, `␣-` compete with `␣"`.

On a production GLM-5.3 deployment this corrupted **26.5%** of `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}` responses, returning a number where the first string value belonged:

{"location": 0.2373, "temperature": 12, ...}
{"location": 0,      "temperature": 0, ... "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"}

On Blackwell (SM100/SM110) with `head_size == head_size_v == 256`, FA4 dispatches its dedicated hd256 kernel, which asserts `not is_split_kv`. Once the batch is large enough for the split-KV heuristic to fire, that assertion trips and takes down the engine core.

This affects `glm_moe_dsa` models (GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3 family), whose `v_head_dim` is 256.

## Symptom

```
assert not is_split_kv, "SM100 forward with head_dim=256 does not support SplitKV"
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed / engine core proc died
```

Reproduced on 4x B200 (TP=4), `max_model_len 32768`, GLM-5.2 NVFP4: serving is stable at low load and the engine dies once concurrency reaches roughly 32. Below that threshold the heuristic does not split, which is why this does not show up in small smoke tests.

## Root cause

The dense FA path already knows this kernel cannot split — `uses_fa4_hd256_kernel` exists in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/fa_utils.py` and is consulted in `flash_attn.py`. The sparse MLA call site is the one place that builds FA4 kwargs for the same kernel without the corresponding guard.

## Fix

Pin `num_splits = 1` when the hd256 kernel is in play, reusing the existing helper rather than hardcoding the head size:

```python
if uses_fa4_hd256_kernel(q.shape[-1], v.shape[-1]):
    kwargs["num_splits"] = 1
```

The helper already checks the device capability (major in `(10, 11)`), so this is a no-op on every other platform and on every other head size. No behaviour change outside the configuration that currently crashes.

## Test

Verified on `v0.29.0` with the equivalent guard applied to the same call site: the engine survives a concurrency sweep of 8 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 256 with zero failed requests, where the unpatched build dies at 32. The change in this PR is rebased onto `main` and switched to the existing helper; I do not have a Blackwell box
